rev1_reasons_resolved: The -g line-table change is fixed. be24841f69b7 adds isMeta = 1 to PseudoLOOPend (RISCVInstrInfoXpulp.td:752), and f9b9b624d165 builds the marker with an empty DebugLoc (PULPFixupHwLoops.cpp:765). The worker's claim that isMeta alone was not enough (DwarfDebug::findForceIsStmtInstrs uses the last instruction in a block that has a DebugLoc, meta or not) fits my earlier seed-7043 result: row count unchanged, two rows lost is_stmt. The two-part fix is justified.
The asm-printer remark counts are fixed as well (isMeta).
The note covers -g in 'Why this is equivalent' (line 22) and gives an observable symptom in 'What breaks' (line 29).

checks_done.empty_debugloc_meta_terminator: Harmless. (a) The verifier has no DebugLoc requirement: 0 'Bad machine' errors everywhere above. (b) llc -debugify-and-strip-all-safe -verify-machineinstrs (MIR debugify before each pass) passes on xpulp-hwloop-countdown/-layout/-obj and xpulp-postinc-f32 with hardware loops formed; int-20 aborts in the verifier on the same inputs. (c) llc -debugify-check-and-strip-all-safe asserts in MachineCheckDebugify.cpp:86 ('Unexpected name for DILocalVariable'), identically in int-20, also with -mattr=+m,+c (no xpulp) and with -stop-before=hwloopsfixup: an upstream debugify-check issue with these inputs, not this change. (d) -O0: llc -O0 still forms a hardware loop in xpulp-hwloop-layout.ll/-obj and is verifier-clean; clang -O0 -g fuzz objects are identical. (e) Branch analysis: RISCVInstrInfo::analyzeBranch checks the opcode before anything else, so isMeta does not affect the 'unanalyzable' result. isUnpredicatedTerminator and getFirstTerminator do not skip meta instructions. getInstSizeInBytes returns 0 on its first line for meta instructions. The fixup pass's own isMetaInstruction/isTransient skips only step over a zero-size terminator, so its offsets are unchanged. (f) The AsmPrinter still calls RISCVAsmPrinter::emitInstruction for the meta pseudo, and that case returns without emitting.

rev1_checks_done.rules_upstream: No upstream commit caused this. It is a pre-existing fork defect, and the cited fork commit f1b7aebff8c2 (Ficarelli 2022-08-25) exists and is the only hit of git log pulp/integer_SIMD_fix -S'setLabelMustBeEmitted' on PULPFixupHwLoops.cpp. Reference code checked at llvmorg-20.1.8: HexagonPseudo.td:90-100 ENDLOOP0/1 (isBranch, isTerminator), HexagonMCInstLower.cpp:98-105 (ENDLOOP0 sets the packet's inner-loop parse bits and emits no word of its own, so the note's 'no instruction word' is accurate; note that Hexagon's analyzeBranch does understand ENDLOOP, which Hexagon needs because its marker exists before branch folding, and PULP's does not), ARMBaseInstrInfo.cpp:405-417 (generic 'unrecognized terminator' bail-out that also covers t2LoopEnd when the pipeliner is off). The citations are fair.
rev1_checks_done.oracle_cheating: No fork logic was removed and no early return was added in a way that drops a feature. The analyzeBranch early return only reports 'unanalyzable' for the new marker. LOOPsetup definitions are unchanged. The removed LivePhysRegs block in splitMBBAt is replaced by computeAndAddLiveIns, not deleted. No test was edited. Every hunk serves one of the four verifier findings.
rev1_checks_done.design_post_pass_safety: PULPFixupHwLoops runs in RISCVPassConfig::addPreEmitPass2 (RISCVTargetMachine.cpp:583). In TargetPassConfig::addMachinePasses, branch folding, block placement, tail duplication, post-RA scheduling, MachineCopyPropagation, BranchRelaxation, RISCVMakeCompressible (addPreEmitPass, line 1204) and the MachineOutliner (line 1228) all run earlier. After it come only RISCVExpandAtomicPseudo (which splits blocks with transferSuccessors, keeps the marker, and uses no analyzeBranch), UnpackMachineBundles and the AsmPrinter. So no pass can move, delete or size-account the marker after insertion. getInstSizeInBytes(PseudoLOOPend) = 0: it has no compress pattern, so the default case returns desc Size = 0. AsmPrinter::isBlockOnlyReachableByFallthrough of the exit block is unchanged (marker is a direct branch to the header, not the exit), which is why the loop-exit label emission is unchanged. The marker is not a barrier, so the verifier still allows fallthrough to the exit.
rev1_checks_done.known_gaps_nonblocking: (i) MLI is not updated for blocks the pass creates. If a hardware loop's LastMBB were a LoopEnd block made earlier in the same pass, getLoopFor returns null and no marker is placed. The verifier would then complain; no silent miscompile. Never seen in fuzzing. (ii) Padding when lp.setup is not the last instruction of its block (inspt != end) still puts nops between terminators. Not seen. (iii) The third pass's range-for visits the new PadMBB with offset 0. Harmless, because it holds only nops.

The same 72 builds fail in both (Sema/shim, the known -file TUs). New build: 162/162 verifier-clean.
rev1_checks_done.fuzz_compile_objects: Seeds 5001-6500 (not in the worker's range) x {O2, O3, Os, O3 -mrelax, O2 and O3 with -pulp-loop-range-immediate=0} = 9000 builds. All 9000 are whole-ELF byte-identical to base after removing .comment, and all are verifier-clean. 8242 contain lp.setup; 2330 contain padding nops right after lp.setup.
rev1_checks_done.gvsoc_short_loops: 100 random seeds whose O3 -pulp-loop-range-immediate=0 build has nop-padded loops, run with the adapted one.sh (NEW = 20-F013 snapshot, BASE = int-20 snapshot, plus an object compare) x O2/O3/Os = 300 GVSoC runs against GAP9 GCC. All objects are identical to base, with 0 hangs and 0 crashes. 297 OK. Seed 6012 mismatches GCC at all three levels. This is pre-existing and not about hardware loops: a clang -march=rv32imc_zfinx build (no xpulp) gives the same result as the PULP build, 0xb1ae795c 0xa7f363b3, while GCC gives 0xba0be6dc 0x328ffe39, so the likely cause is generator UB or a GCC-side difference. Because the objects are identical, lp.setup start/end labels bracket the same bytes as before, and loops padded to the 2-instruction minimum are unchanged. The asm difference is only the new PadMBB label line '.LBBx_y:' before the nops, plus renumbered %bb comments.
